chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqda told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Mufaddal ibn Qays ibn Rummana al-Ash'ari, Sa'dan ibn Ishaq ibn Sa'id, Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Malik, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Qatawani all told us: They narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub al-Zarrad from Hisham ibn Salim, from Yazeed al-Kinasi, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him) saying:
The master of this matter has a likeness to Joseph (peace be upon him); he is the son of a black bondmaid. Allah will set his affairs right in a single night.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The Master of the Command (referring to the Mahdi)
key_terms.يُصْلِحُ اللَّهُ لَهُ أَمْرَهُ: Allah will set his affairs right/establish his cause

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the comparison between the Mahdi and Prophet Joseph in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the Mahdi’s lineage through his mother, often identified as Nargis or Sumayyah, a bondmaid of African origin, drawing a direct typological parallel to Prophet Joseph’s rise from obscurity to power. The phrase 'rectifies his affairs in a single night' underscores the concept of *Fath al-Mubarram* (the decisive victory), suggesting a rapid and divinely accelerated establishment of justice, mirroring Joseph’s sudden elevation in Egypt. This comparison serves to reassure the Shia community of the Mahdi’s legitimacy and the swift, miraculous nature of his reappearance.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (8) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed bin Oqda narrated from Muhammad bin al-Mufadhdhal bin Qayss bin Rummana al-Ash’ari, Sa’dan bin Iss’haq bin Sa’eed, Ahmad bin al-Husayn bin Abdul Melik and Muhammad bin al-Hasan al-Qatawani all from al-Hasan bin Mahboob az-Zarrad from Hisham bin Salim from Yazeed al-Kinasi that Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) had said:

“The man of this matter has a likeness to Prophet Joseph (as). He is a son of a (black) bondmaid. Allah will make him succeed within a night.” The likeness to Prophet Joseph (as) concerns the disappearance.
